newsitem.title: USA: Fox and Liberty sports venture to spend US850 million.
newsitem.headline: Fox and Liberty sports venture to spend US850 million.

text.p: Fox/Liberty Networks has agreed to invest $850 million for a 40 percent stake in Rainbow Media Holdings Inc's sports interests, the companies said Monday.
The companies will form an equally owned national sports television programming venture that will reach 55 million homes under the name FOX Sports Net.

Also, Fox/Liberty will contribute $850 million for a 40 percent equity interest in a new joint venture that will own Rainbow's regional sports networks, which operate under the name SportsChannel, and the Madison Square Garden business.
Fox/Liberty is a joint venture of News Corp's Fox Sports unit and Liberty Media Corp.
Liberty Media is a unit of Tele-Communications Inc.
Rainbow is 75 percent owned by Cablevision Systems Corp and 25 percent owned by General Electric Co's NBC unit.
Fox/Liberty said it will raise the $850 million through a third-party bank loan.
Rainbow will use the proceeds to significantly reduce debt.
Rainbow will maintain management control of its current regional sports networks, but they will be re-branded under the Fox Sports banner, with the exception of MSG Network and SportsChannel Florida.

The new TV venture, to include national, regional and local sports programming, will appear on nine Fox/Liberty regional cable TV networks, eight Rainbow regional sports channels, and the Fox Sports regional sports systems.
Rainbow will also maintain management control of Madison Square Garden, including the Knicks and Rangers, the MSG network and the arena complex.

Rupert Murdoch, chief executive of News Corp, said, "This is a major step in providing a real national sports network under the Fox name with Fox quality. Viewers will now have Fox Sports programming on a local and national level, which viewers have long desired."
Marc Lustgarten, Cablevision vice chairman, said, "This new network will be an unparalleled source of regional and national televised sports programming..."
Cablevision Chief Executive James Dolan said the deal "represents a significant step forward in Cablevision's overall financial strategy of reducing leverage and focusing on our core businesses."
Separately, Cablevision said Lustgarten was named chairman of the board of Madison Square Garden. Fox/Liberty will have no management role in the MSG entities.
